title: Three.js Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Three.js course.

entries.name: Draw your first cube
entries.summary: A mesh joins a shape with a material. The scene holds the mesh, and the renderer draws it from the camera's view.

entries.name: Move the camera
entries.summary: The camera is the viewpoint into a scene.

entries.name: Choose a different geometry
entries.summary: Geometry describes an object's shape. A sphere geometry uses small triangles to approximate a round surface.

entries.name: Show the shape as lines
entries.summary: A material tells the renderer how a shape should look.

entries.name: Place an object
entries.summary: An object's position moves it along three scene axes: x, y and z.

entries.name: Turn an object
entries.summary: Rotation turns an object around an axis.

entries.name: Resize an object with scale
entries.summary: Scale multiplies an object's size on each axis.

entries.name: Move a group together
entries.summary: A Group can hold several objects. Moving the group moves all its children together.

entries.name: Light a shaded material
entries.summary: Some materials respond to light. MeshStandardMaterial needs lighting so its surfaces can show shape and shading.

entries.name: Animate using time
entries.summary: An animation loop draws new frames. Using elapsed time makes motion less dependent on how many frames the device can draw.

entries.name: Resize the camera view
entries.summary: A perspective camera needs the canvas aspect ratio.

entries.name: Clean up a scene
entries.summary: GPU resources need explicit cleanup when a scene is no longer used.
